strengths: Addresses an increasingly critical practical bottleneck in video generative modeling: as DiT inference becomes faster through distillation and few-step sampling, VAE decoding dominates overall latency.

The proposed method is well-grounded in empirical profiling and analysis, namely the observation of low-rank channel redundancy via SVD and the resolution-dependent computational overhead of CausalConv3D operations.

The technical design is cohesive and elegant: the greedy R^2-based channel selection, the channel expressivity loss with gradient masking, and the topology-preserving 1x1 shortcut initialization resolve non-trivial architectural continuity issues in residual networks.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple VAE backbones (Wan 2.1, LTX-Video), multiple datasets (UCF-101, DAVIS 2019), edge and desktop hardware (Jetson Orin, RTX 5090D), and end-to-end text-to-video generation frameworks (Self-Forcing, FastVideo) using VBench-2.0.
weaknesses: The stage-wise operator substitution (3D depthwise separable conv vs. 2D conv) and layer-specific pruning ratios (e.g., 1/8 for Wan 2.1 vs. 1/4 for LTX-Video) are manually configured rather than determined via an automated, architecture-agnostic search or sensitivity analysis.

Comparisons with baselines like LightVAE and Turbo-VAED lack explicit details regarding training compute parity (e.g., whether baselines were retrained on the same curated 10K dataset with equivalent GPU hours).

Replacing 3D convolutions with 2D convolutions in the high-resolution stages can limit temporal high-frequency reconstruction, which, as noted in the limitations, leads to noticeable blur or degradation on rapidly moving fine objects and faces.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely bottleneck: as diffusion transformer (DiT) inference latency drops rapidly with few-step distillation and acceleration techniques, the VAE decoder becomes the dominant computational bottleneck (accounting for 30-40% of total pipeline latency).

Technically sound and principled design: the independence-aware channel pruning leverages singular value decomposition (SVD) and $R^2$ linear reconstructability rather than naive magnitude or pairwise similarity, coupled with a clever topology-preserving $1 \times 1$ shortcut injection to resolve residual continuity issues.

Well-justified operator optimization: replacing CausalConv3D with 3D depthwise separable convolutions in deep/low-resolution stages and 2D convolutions in shallow/high-resolution stages is both theoretically motivated and empirically validated.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: demonstrated across two leading open video VAEs (Wan 2.1 and LTX-Video), tested on both desktop GPUs (RTX 5090D) and edge devices (Jetson Orin), evaluated on UCF-101, DAVIS 2019, and full generation benchmarks (VBench-2.0) with significant speedups (~6x decoder speedup, up to 36% end-to-end speedup) and minimal fidelity loss.
Thorough ablation studies verifying the contributions of each stage of the three-phase dynamic distillation framework, projection initialization, and pruning criteria.
weaknesses: Baseline asymmetry across backbones: Turbo-VAED is compared only on LTX-Video while LightVAE is compared on Wan 2.1. It would strengthen the paper to evaluate Turbo-VAED on Wan 2.1 (or explicitly clarify any baseline availability/compatibility limitations).

Heuristic layer-wise configuration: the selection of which layers are replaced with 2D convolutions versus 3D DW convolutions, and the exact channel pruning ratios per stage, appears to rely on manual heuristics per model family rather than an automated or unified architecture-search/budget-allocation criterion.

Discussion of limitations on high-frequency temporal dynamics: as noted in Appendix B.9, the decoder can struggle with dense high-frequency motion and facial details due to the reduced capacity, though this is an inherent and understandable trade-off for such extreme compression.

strengths: Addresses an increasingly critical bottleneck in modern generative video pipelines: as diffusion transformer (DiT) denoisers are accelerated via few-step distillation, the VAE decoding latency becomes a dominant factor (accounting for up to 30-40% of end-to-end latency).

Principled architectural modifications motivated by empirical analysis: replacing computationally dominant CausalConv3D with 3D depthwise separable convolutions in deep layers, transitioning to 2D convolutions in high-resolution shallow layers after temporal upsampling, and resolving residual shortcut mismatch via topology-preserving linear least-squares projection.
Independence-aware channel pruning leverages singular value decomposition (SVD) and R^2 explained variance rather than brittle pairwise similarity, effectively capturing channel redundancy.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple strong backbones (Wan 2.1 and LTX-Video), consumer and edge hardware (RTX 5090D and Jetson AGX Orin), diverse benchmarks (UCF-101, DAVIS 2019 at 720p, VBench-2.0), and multiple accelerated generation frameworks (Self-Forcing, FastVideo, Causal Forcing).
Detailed ablation studies validate individual design choices, including the three-phase dynamic distillation strategy, shortcut projection matrix initialization, and pruning criteria.
weaknesses: The underlying technical components (depthwise separable convolutions, 3D-to-2D stage conversion, feature distillation, and least-squares reconstruction pruning akin to ThiNet) are individually established techniques, making the primary novelty lie in system integration and empirical tailoring for video VAEs.

Architectural decisions are manually customized per backbone rather than discovered automatically via a unified search policy (e.g., Wan 2.1 applies 1/8 pruning on up2/up3, while LTX-Video retains up2 as 3D and applies 1/4 pruning on up2/up3).

The three-phase training pipeline relies on five loss components (L1, LPIPS, SSIM, distillation, expressivity) and phase-dependent adaptation layers, introducing hyperparameter tuning complexity when extending to new architectures.

Evaluation on non-causal or transformer-based video autoencoders is restricted to preliminary discussion and exploratory SVD/latency estimates in the appendix, without full end-to-end training and generation validation.
